transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh, yeah… I guess the main thing is I can’t stay on track. Like I’ll sit down to work on an application or something, and then suddenly every little thing pulls me away — a car outside, my phone lighting up, or even just some random thought. And then I’m off doing something else before I even realize I stopped.

It’s frustrating because I’ll start with good intentions, you know? Like I’ll have the page open and everything, and then… I don’t know, I remember some totally unrelated thing or hear something outside, and I’m gone.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah, pretty often. Like if I’m sitting with someone, my leg’s usually bouncing and I don’t even notice until they look at it or something. Or I’ll be clicking a pen, messing with my keys… actually I’ve had people get annoyed by the pen clicking before, so I try not to, but then I just end up doing something else with my hands.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah… I think so. Like, I’ll cut people off a lot. Especially my mom, or like when I’m talking to the counselor, because an answer pops into my head and I just say it before they’re even done talking.

And then sometimes I realize after, like, oh, they were still saying something. My mom gets annoyed because she’ll be trying to explain something and I’m already jumping in, and then we kind of get off track… which, I mean, happens a lot with us anyway, but yeah, I guess that’s the main thing.
Have you ever done something without thinking that put you or others in danger?

Um… I don’t know. Not that I can think of, like, danger-danger. I mean, I’ve done dumb stuff where afterward I’m like, “Why did I do that?” but I’m not sure if it’s the kind of thing you mean.

Like sometimes I’ll say something without thinking and it causes a whole argument, but that’s not really dangerous, I guess. When you say danger, do you mean like driving or getting hurt or something?
Do you have trouble focusing or staying on task at work or in school?

Yeah, I do. Like even with stuff I’m trying to learn, like if I’m watching a repair video or reading the manual for some tool, I’ll start out paying attention, and then a few minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at it.

Then I have to back the video up or reread the same part because I didn’t take in any of it. It’s annoying because I’ll think I’m focused, but then nothing actually stuck.
Have you always had trouble paying attention and staying on track, even when you were a kid?

Yeah, I think so. Like, even back in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d be talking when I wasn’t supposed to.

And I’d forget homework a lot, which I remember because my backpack was just… a mess. Papers everywhere. I’d find stuff weeks later, like, oh, that was due already. And on worksheets I’d rush through them and make stupid mistakes, even when I knew the answers.

It’s funny, I can still picture one classroom where they moved me near the teacher’s desk, and I hated that because everyone could see— but yeah, it’s kind of been like that since I was little.
Do you have intense mood swings, where you feel extremely happy, angry, or sad, that seem to come out of nowhere?

I don’t know if I’d call them intense mood swings. I mean, I get irritated sometimes, like anybody, and there are days where I’m in a bad mood and I’m not even totally sure why.

But “extremely happy” or “extremely sad” out of nowhere… I’m not sure. Like, I’ll get annoyed if something stupid happens, like if I can’t find my keys, and then I’m tearing the whole room apart and getting more frustrated because I swear I just had them. Actually, my room’s been kind of a disaster lately—well, not lately, kind of always—but I don’t think that’s what you mean.

So… yeah, I guess I haven’t really noticed big mood swings like that.
Do you feel like your difficulties with attention and impulsivity are causing problems in your relationships or daily life?

Yeah… it is causing problems, mostly with just getting my life moving, I guess. Like I keep trying to get on track with becoming an automotive technician, because I know I’m good with the hands-on stuff—cars make sense to me when I’m actually working on them.

But then there’s all the other stuff around it, like training deadlines or applications, and I’ll miss something or mess it up and have to redo it. And then I’m stuck in the same place again. It’s frustrating because it’s not like I don’t want to do it. I do. I just keep tripping over the paperwork and deadlines before I even get to the part I’m actually good at.
Have you experienced these attention and impulsivity issues consistently throughout your life, including as a child, teenager, and adult?

Yeah, I mean… it goes way back. I was just talking about elementary school, but that’s really when it was obvious. Teachers kept moving my seat around because I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, like I’d just blurt stuff out or start chatting.

And the homework thing was constant. I’d forget it, or it’d be somewhere in my backpack, which was always like this black hole of crumpled papers. I remember finding worksheets later and being like, oh, that was already due. And even when I knew the work, I’d rush through it and make dumb mistakes, just because I wanted to be done.

So yeah… I don’t think it suddenly started as an adult. It’s kind of been there since I was a kid.
Do you feel like your difficulties with attention and impulsivity are causing significant stress or problems for you?

Yeah… I mean, it’s definitely stressing me out. It’s not just like, “oh I forgot something once.” I’ve missed training deadlines and had to redo applications more than once, and it keeps putting me back at the start.

Like with the automotive technician stuff—when I’m actually around cars or doing hands-on work, I feel like I can do that. That part makes sense. But then the forms, deadlines, checking everything, submitting things on time… I mess that part up, and then nothing moves forward. It’s frustrating because I know I’m not lazy about the actual work. It just feels like I keep getting stuck before I even get to it.
Do you have trouble sitting still or behaving calmly in quiet environments, like in a library or during a movie?

Yeah, quiet stuff is hard for me. Like if my family’s watching a movie, I’ll start talking during it or I’ll get up for no real reason, or I’ll be making some kind of noise and not even realize I’m doing it.

Same thing if I try to sit and read. I’ll be there for a few minutes and then I’m shifting around or messing with something. I don’t mean to bother people, but it comes out that way sometimes.
Do you think your problems with staying on track and being easily distracted are more bothersome to you than your restlessness and impulsive behaviors?

Yeah, I think the getting distracted part bothers me more, honestly. The restless stuff is annoying, but the main thing is I’ll be trying to stay on one thing—like an application or some paperwork—and then every little thing pulls me away.

Like a car goes by outside, or my phone lights up, or I’ll have some random thought like, “oh, I should look that up,” and then I’m somewhere else before I even realize I stopped doing the original thing. And then by the time I come back to it, I’ve lost where I was. That’s the part that really messes me up.
Have your difficulties with attention and impulsivity caused problems in your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah, somewhat. I don’t think I’m trying to be rude, but I do cut people off a lot. Like with my mom especially, or even my counselor, they’ll be explaining something and an answer pops into my head and I just say it before they’re even done.

Then afterward I’m like, “Why did I do that?” because it makes it seem like I’m not listening, even if I actually am. My mom gets annoyed by it, and I get it. It’s like I’m worried I’ll lose the thought if I don’t say it right then… which, actually, that happens with other stuff too, like when I’m trying to remember something from earlier—but yeah, with relationships, it mostly shows up as me interrupting people.
Have you experienced these difficulties with attention and impulsivity in multiple settings, such as at home, at work, or in social situations?

Yeah, it’s not just one place. Like, at home it shows up, but the bigger one is with trying to move forward with work stuff—well, not work exactly, I’m not working right now, but trying to get into being an automotive technician.

I know I can do the hands-on part. Like when I’m actually around cars and tools, that makes sense to me. But the training deadlines and applications and all that paperwork-type stuff… I’ve missed deadlines, or I’ll fill something out wrong and have to redo it, and then it sets me back again. It’s happened enough that I’m still kind of stuck instead of actually moving forward, which is frustrating because it’s not like I don’t want to do it.
Have you had to change jobs or significantly alter your daily routines because of your difficulties with attention and impulsivity?

Yeah, I haven’t really changed jobs because I’m not working right now, but it’s definitely changed what my days look like. Like, I keep having to go back and redo applications or fix stuff I filled out wrong, and I’ve missed training deadlines more than once.

It’s frustrating because with the automotive technician thing, I feel like if I could just get through the paperwork and the deadline part, I’d be fine. I like being around cars, and the hands-on work makes sense to me—like, I can focus better when I’m actually doing that. But all the steps to get there keep getting messed up, so I’m kind of still stuck in the same place instead of moving forward.
Have you ever had to significantly adjust your daily life or occupation because of your difficulties with attention and impulsivity?

Yeah, I guess I have, more than I want to admit. It’s mostly with trying to get into the automotive technician stuff. Like, I know I can do the actual hands-on work—when I’m around cars, tools, engines, that kind of thing, I feel way more like myself.

But the application parts and training deadlines, that’s where I keep messing up. I’ve missed deadlines, or I’ll send something in wrong and then have to redo it, and by the time I fix it I’m already behind. So it’s like my whole day ends up being about fixing some form or figuring out what I forgot to submit, instead of actually moving forward.

And then I get frustrated because I’m still not really getting started, even though the thing I want to do is right there.
Do you think your difficulties with restlessness and impulsivity are as bothersome to you as your difficulties with staying focused and on track?

Yeah… I mean, the restlessness and impulsive stuff is annoying, but honestly the focus thing bothers me more. Like, I’ll be trying to work on an application, and then every little thing pulls me off—my phone buzzes, or a car goes by outside, or I suddenly remember some random thing I wanted to look up.

And then before I even realize it, I’m not doing the application anymore. I’m off on something else, and then I come back and I’m like, wait, what was I even filling out? That’s the part that really messes me up.
Have you noticed any changes in how often you experience these difficulties with attention and impulsivity as you've grown older?

Yeah, I mean… it feels like it’s been there since I was little, just looks different now, I guess. Like in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d talk out of turn or get distracted by whoever was next to me.

I also forgot homework a lot, or I’d rush through worksheets and make dumb mistakes I probably could’ve avoided if I slowed down. I remember getting in trouble for that, and then I’d be like, “Okay, I’ll do better,” but then the same thing would happen again.

Now it’s more with applications and deadlines and stuff, but it kind of feels like the same problem wearing different clothes.
Do you think your difficulties with attention, impulsivity, and restlessness are equally problematic for you, or does one area stand out as more troublesome?

The attention part stands out the most, I think. Like, the main thing is I get pulled off track by every little thing.

I’ll be trying to work on an application, and then a car outside goes by, or my phone makes a noise, or I’ll have some random thought like, “Oh, I should look that up,” and then suddenly I’m somewhere else completely. Sometimes I don’t even notice I’ve left what I was doing until later.

The restlessness is there too, but getting distracted like that is what really messes me up day to day.
Have you experienced difficulties with attention and impulsivity in all aspects of your life, including work, school, and social situations, consistently over time?

Yeah, it’s kind of been across everything, but… the really disruptive version of it has been going on for about, I guess, a year and ten months now. Since I hurt myself playing soccer and got knocked out of my normal routine.

Before that I had stuff too, but after the injury it was like everything got harder to keep together. And it’s weird because soccer used to structure my day, you know? Like practices, games, where I had to be at a certain time… even my friends were kind of tied into that. Then suddenly that was gone, and I just didn’t have the same rhythm. So yeah, since then it’s been pretty consistently messing with me.

doctor.question: Do you think your difficulties with restlessness and impulsivity are as bothersome to you as your difficulties with staying focused and on track?

target_item.name: Distractibility
target_item.manifestation: The main thing is I get pulled off track by every little sound or thought, like I’ll be trying to work on an application and then a car outside, my phone, or some random idea sends me somewhere else before I even notice.
target_item.reason: The doctor is comparing restlessness/impulsivity with difficulties staying focused and on track; the most direct profile item for staying focused and being pulled off track is distractibility.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, the restlessness and impulsive stuff is annoying, but honestly the focus thing bothers me more. Like, I’ll be trying to work on an application, and then every little thing pulls me off—my phone buzzes, or a car goes by outside, or I suddenly remember some random thing I wanted to look up.

And then before I even realize it, I’m not doing the application anymore. I’m off on something else, and then I come back and I’m like, wait, what was I even filling out? That’s the part that really messes me up.

doctor.intent: determine if symptoms have persisted into adulthood consistently
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in how often you experience these difficulties with attention and impulsivity as you've grown older?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Even in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat because I talked out of turn, forgot homework, and rushed through worksheets with careless mistakes.
target_item.reason: The question asks about how the attention and impulsivity difficulties have changed over development/growing older, which is most directly related to childhood onset and lifelong pattern.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean… it feels like it’s been there since I was little, just looks different now, I guess. Like in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d talk out of turn or get distracted by whoever was next to me.

I also forgot homework a lot, or I’d rush through worksheets and make dumb mistakes I probably could’ve avoided if I slowed down. I remember getting in trouble for that, and then I’d be like, “Okay, I’ll do better,” but then the same thing would happen again.

Now it’s more with applications and deadlines and stuff, but it kind of feels like the same problem wearing different clothes.

doctor.intent: determine if symptoms meet criteria for a specific attention deficit hyperactivity disorder subtype
doctor.question: Do you think your difficulties with attention, impulsivity, and restlessness are equally problematic for you, or does one area stand out as more troublesome?

target_item.name: Distractibility
target_item.manifestation: The main thing is I get pulled off track by every little sound or thought, like I’ll be trying to work on an application and then a car outside, my phone, or some random idea sends me somewhere else before I even notice.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking which area stands out as most troublesome among attention, impulsivity, and restlessness. Based on the dialogue, staying focused and being pulled off track is the main difficulty, matching distractibility.

patient.answer:
The attention part stands out the most, I think. Like, the main thing is I get pulled off track by every little thing.

I’ll be trying to work on an application, and then a car outside goes by, or my phone makes a noise, or I’ll have some random thought like, “Oh, I should look that up,” and then suddenly I’m somewhere else completely. Sometimes I don’t even notice I’ve left what I was doing until later.

The restlessness is there too, but getting distracted like that is what really messes me up day to day.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms have persisted consistently across different settings and times
doctor.question: Have you experienced difficulties with attention and impulsivity in all aspects of your life, including work, school, and social situations, consistently over time?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: It’s been this disruptive for about 1 year and 10 months, ever since my soccer injury knocked me out of my usual routine.
target_item.reason: The question is mainly asking whether the attention and impulsivity difficulties have been consistent over time, which is best captured by the duration item.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it’s kind of been across everything, but… the really disruptive version of it has been going on for about, I guess, a year and ten months now. Since I hurt myself playing soccer and got knocked out of my normal routine.

Before that I had stuff too, but after the injury it was like everything got harder to keep together. And it’s weird because soccer used to structure my day, you know? Like practices, games, where I had to be at a certain time… even my friends were kind of tied into that. Then suddenly that was gone, and I just didn’t have the same rhythm. So yeah, since then it’s been pretty consistently messing with me.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity have been persistent since childhood, causing significant distress and impairment in social, occupational, and other areas of life.
